prompt: In the tasks API's route table, which HTTP method is used to update an existing task at /tasks/:id?
choices: GET
POST
PUT
DELETE

prompt: A client successfully creates a new task via POST /tasks. What HTTP status code should the server return?
A client sends POST /tasks with a body of {} (no title field at all). What should the server respond with?
choices: 500 Internal Server Error, because the database insert failed
400 Bad Request, with an error message explaining title is required
201 Created, with title set to null
404 Not Found

prompt: A client requests GET /tasks/999 and no task with id 999 exists. What is the correct status code?
After a successful DELETE /tasks/1, which response is correct for this API?
choices: 200 with the deleted task's data in the body
204 with an empty body
202 with a confirmation message
201 with an empty body

prompt: Why does the SQLite example use db.prepare('SELECT * FROM tasks WHERE id = ?').get(id) instead of building the query with string concatenation like `'SELECT * FROM tasks WHERE id = ' + id`?
choices: Parameter placeholders run faster in every case
String concatenation only works with better-sqlite3, not Python's sqlite3 module
Placeholders let the database library safely escape the value, preventing SQL injection
It is required syntax in SQLite and concatenated queries will not execute

prompt: In the Express server, what does app.use(express.json()) do?
choices: It connects the app to the SQLite database
It parses incoming JSON request bodies so they are available as a plain object on req.body
It converts every response into JSON automatically, including HTML routes
It validates that incoming JSON matches a defined schema
